clue.text: Polish worker given start by chess player

parts.note: to boot a computer is to start it up
Black is one of the two players in a game of chess, the one with the dark pieces

explanation.surface: A labourer from Poland gets an opening move from a chess opponent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' looks like a nationality but is the verb: the worker polishes shoes.
explanation.definitionFit: A bootblack is someone who shines shoes for a living, so a worker whose job is polish.

clue.text: Cook has to cook without recipe

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the cooking word goes around the recipe letter

parts.note: to boil is to cook in water
R is the abbreviation for recipe, from the Latin 'take' on prescriptions

explanation.surface: A chef forced to cook with no recipe to follow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, not lacking: R sits inside BOIL.
explanation.definitionFit: To broil is to grill, a way of cooking food under direct heat.

clue.text: Unconventional set — cool cats

indicators.note: something unconventional departs from the usual order, so these letters are put in a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A group of unusual, hip jazz people described as cool cats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unconventional' rearranges SET and COOL together; 'cool cats' reads as slang for hip people, but only 'cats' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Ocelots are wild spotted felines of the Americas.

clue.text: Plants grown for money, cropped in case

parts.note: brass is British slang for money

indicators.note: cropped means cut short, so each of the two words loses its last letter

explanation.surface: Crops grown for profit are cut back as a precaution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cropped' trims both IN and CASE, leaving I and CAS after BRASS; 'grown for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Brassicas are the cabbage family of vegetables, such as kale and sprouts.

clue.text: Tweak charged particle, causing dispute

parts.note: to tweak something is to alter it slightly
a cation is a positively charged ion

explanation.surface: Adjusting an electrically charged particle leads to an argument in the lab.
explanation.definitionFit: An altercation is a noisy quarrel or argument.

clue.text: Tackle Marlowe

definitions.meaning: tackle is gear or equipment, as in fishing tackle

explanation.definitionFit: Kit means equipment or gear, as fishing tackle is; and Kit was the familiar name of the playwright Christopher Marlowe.

clue.text: Indian gentleman starts to seek all Hindus in Bangalore

indicators.note: the starts of the following words are taken, one initial letter from each

explanation.surface: A traveller seeking out all the Hindus in a southern Indian city.
explanation.definitionFit: Sahib was a respectful form of address for a man of standing in colonial India.

clue.text: Finch from southern Ireland

parts.note: Erin is a poetic name for Ireland

explanation.surface: A small bird arriving from the south of Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: The serin is a small yellow-green European songbird of the finch family.

clue.text: Leaflet dismissed by worker

indicators.note: by means next to, so the dismissal word stands beside the worker word

parts.note: a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand
a batsman dismissed in cricket is out

explanation.surface: A pamphlet thrown away by an employee.
explanation.definitionFit: A handout is a printed sheet given out free, such as a flyer.

clue.text: Swaggering dandies, stylish in red

parts.note: a blood is an old word for a fashionable, swaggering young man about town
hot means very fashionable or in vogue

explanation.surface: Showy young dandies dressed smartly in red.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link; 'red' is the definition, as in eyes that are red.
explanation.definitionFit: Bloodshot eyes are reddened by swollen blood vessels.

clue.text: About to carve ham

indicators.note: about suggests the letters are turned around and put in a different order

explanation.surface: Someone preparing to slice a joint of ham.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ham' looks like the meat on the carving board but is the theatrical verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To ham is to perform in an exaggerated, theatrical manner.

clue.text: Piano dispatched promptly to leading city

indicators.note: leading means coming first, so this word goes before the rest

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: dispatched means sent off, so the music letter is removed

parts.note: pronto is informal for promptly, at once
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning soft

explanation.surface: A piano is shipped quickly to a major city.
explanation.definitionFit: Toronto is the largest city in Canada, the capital of Ontario.

clue.text: British sportsmen, they have their pride

definitions.meaning: the touring rugby team drawn from Britain and Ireland
a pride is the collective noun for a group of these big cats

explanation.definitionFit: The British and Irish Lions are a touring rugby union team; big cats live in groups called prides.

clue.text: Plunder in American locality for folk hero

parts.note: to plunder is to rob
taken as written
hood is American slang for neighbourhood

explanation.surface: Looting in a US neighbourhood, done in the name of a popular legend.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary English outlaw of Sherwood Forest robbed the rich to give to the poor.

clue.text: As an Asian, Gandhi's able to spin

indicators.note: spinning letters round sets them in a new order

parts.note: the possessive s counts here as a letter of the fodder

explanation.surface: Gandhi, as an Asian, is skilled at spinning cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: Gandhi famously spun his own cloth, which hides 'spin' as the signal; 'As' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A Bangladeshi is a person from Bangladesh, a South Asian country.

clue.text: Publicity for law centre — extremely dangerous

indicators.note: the centre of the word law is its single middle letter
extremely points to the extremes of the word, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Publicising a law centre is said to be risky.
explanation.definitionFit: Ads, short for advertisements, are paid publicity.

clue.text: A switch between right and left in port

indicators.note: between places the swap word between the two direction letters

parts.note: to switch is to change

explanation.surface: A railway switch set between right and left tracks in a harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: Archangel (Arkhangelsk) is a port on the White Sea in northern Russia.
explanation.definitionFit: Archangel is a major Russian seaport on the White Sea.

clue.text: Some knitting restricts small person

parts.note: to chain someone is to restrict them, so restricts means chains
titch is British slang for a small person

explanation.surface: A piece of knitting that hems in a tiny person.
explanation.definitionFit: A chain stitch is a looped stitch used in crochet, knitting and embroidery.

clue.text: One giving evidence, if ignored, would be more irritable

indicators.note: the clue says that if the two-letter word is ignored the rest would be the irritable word, so that word must hold it inside

parts.note: testier means more irritable
taken as written

explanation.surface: A witness in court who would be crosser if overlooked.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue states the container backwards: 'ignored, would be' says strip the word 'if' out of the answer and the comparative of testy is what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: A testifier is a witness who gives testimony.

clue.text: Cook climbs to see food

indicators.note: to cook figures is to doctor them, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A chef climbs up to look at what is to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' looks like the person or the verb of the kitchen; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Comestibles are things that are edible, a formal word for provisions.

clue.text: Renamed wind is to be windy

indicators.note: to wind is to twist about, so the letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A wind given a new name is called windy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wind' reads as the breeze but is the twisting verb, signalling the anagram; 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To meander is to follow a winding, twisting course, like a river.

clue.text: Quality regularly seen last month

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter, at regular intervals

explanation.surface: Quality was consistently seen last month.
explanation.definitionFit: Ult., short for ultimo, is old business shorthand for the month before this one.

clue.text: Ballerina for all to see on top of ladder — a star

parts.note: U is the British film certificate meaning universal, suitable for all audiences

indicators.note: the top of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a nova is a star that suddenly brightens

explanation.surface: A dancer on display at the top of a ladder, as a star.
explanation.walkthrough: Galina Ulanova was a celebrated Soviet prima ballerina of the Bolshoi.
explanation.definitionFit: Galina Ulanova was a famous Russian prima ballerina.

clue.text: Wild individual beginning to dance with a rock group

parts.note: a band is a group of rock musicians
one means a single individual

indicators.note: the beginning of the word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A lone person starting to dance alongside a rock band.
explanation.definitionFit: Abandoned means uninhibited and unrestrained, as wild behaviour is.

clue.text: Fruit would shortly appear old-fashioned

parts.note: a date is the fruit of the date palm
would is shortened to 'd, as in I'd

explanation.surface: Fruit, it is said, would soon look out of date.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dated has gone out of fashion.

clue.text: Patriarch — one with article in pouch

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: in places the article inside the pouch word

parts.note: a sac is a pouch-like cavity in a plant or animal
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An elderly leader carrying a document in a bag.
explanation.definitionFit: Isaac, son of Abraham, is one of the Old Testament patriarchs.

clue.text: Head of college with girl in form

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: lass is a word for a girl

explanation.surface: The college principal, along with a girl, is in good shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form' is a British school word for a class of pupils.
explanation.definitionFit: In British schools a form is a class, a group of pupils taught together.

clue.text: Try to get wife to share expenses

parts.note: to have a go is to try
Dutch, short for duchess, is cockney slang for a wife

explanation.surface: Trying to persuade a spouse to split the bills.
explanation.walkthrough: In cockney 'my old Dutch' means my wife.
explanation.definitionFit: To go Dutch is to split a bill so each pays their own share.

clue.text: Spanning the Mexican border

indicators.note: spanning means stretching across the two words, so the answer lies across their join

explanation.surface: Something stretching across the frontier of Mexico.
explanation.definitionFit: A hem is the edge of a piece of cloth, folded and sewn.

clue.text: Trip to Australia with a philosopher

parts.note: a spin is a short trip, as a drive in the car
Oz is a nickname for Australia

explanation.surface: A thinker takes a journey down under.
explanation.definitionFit: Baruch Spinoza was a 17th-century Dutch rationalist thinker.

clue.text: You are, so to speak, led out or led on

indicators.note: out means on the outside, so the led letters surround the spoken words

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: so to speak signals letters that sound like the spoken phrase

parts.note: said aloud, the phrase is like the two letters U and R in text-speak

explanation.surface: You are someone who is guided out or guided onward.
explanation.definitionFit: To be lured is to be tempted or enticed into following.

clue.text: Watling Street and Fosse Way, say- Roman aids to travel?

definitions.text: Watling Street and Fosse Way, say

indicators.note: to travel is to move about, so the letters move into a new order

explanation.surface: Two famous English routes described as Roman aids to getting around.
explanation.walkthrough: Watling Street and Fosse Way are ancient Roman roads across England.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are major routes built by the Romans in Britain, examples of principal highways.
